statement: Beam option A is not built: a beam is still an exchange that always reaches its target and is decided by a timed press, not by position.
cost_basis: estimate; nearest comparable is the gravity-well packet's 3 to 5 sessions at about 1M each per increment (docs/ep/proposals/gravity-well.html section 7)
risk: The struggle, the answers and the computer's beam play all hang off the exchange form of the beam, so a rewrite can break them; the beam escape probe at three ranges shows it early.

statement: Signatures are not on Orb's inputs: RT + RB + flick and RT + flick do not exist, RT + B is the only input, and no martial signature exists for either fighter.
risk: A flick with RT held may collide with the stick's plain strikes and the transform chord (LT + RT); a refusal count per input on scripted pads shows it early.
orb_question: Once signatures are on RT + flick, is RT held still the ki charge or the High Intensity switch? Recommendation: keep the charge for Alpha.

statement: No gravity well exists in code: no well, zones, draw, snap or intent read, only two pieces of the LT speed ruling behind switches.
evidence: git grep SimWell|DirIntent -- sim data render tools qa: no result
cost_basis: the packet's own plan: about 28M for increments 0 to 8; increments 0, 3 and 4 alone about 9M (docs/ep/proposals/gravity-well.html section 7)
risk: It replaces the three distance bands every close-fight rule reads; the packet's seam tests and hash-identical-when-off line are the early check.
orb_question: Up close, should your stick move only your own fighter? Recommendation: decide before the well is built, starting from the packet's default.

statement: The move table is incomplete for both fighters: RT + X, Y and A are the plain blow, several A and B cells have no outcome, and the LB, LT and RB rows are shared code with no per-fighter content.
cost_basis: the variety packet prices the stick's depth alone at 13M and leaves the other four stances as their own increment (docs/ep/proposals/combat-variety-packet.html section 4)
risk: The cell count drives the cost; agreeing the table with Orb first (55 cells a fighter or a smaller Alpha table) keeps it bounded.
orb_question: Is Alpha's bar the full table (55 cells a fighter) or the martial and energy rows complete with the other rows shared? Recommendation: the smaller table for Alpha, the full one for Beta.
depends_on: data/combat has no owns line; placed by Combat's charter (docs/directors/combat-choreography.md:18-22)

statement: Most of the combat Orb played is off in main's data and on only through the build page's switch rows, so no committed data set is the Alpha's combat.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (each flip changes the hash and needs a golden window and the gate set)
risk: Flipping about 40 combat switches at once hides which one broke a gate; landing them in the page's stack order shows it.

statement: A released stick beam that cannot start waits up to 90 ticks and then fires into whatever the player is doing; open since Orb's last play.
risk: Dropping the wait may make beams feel refused more often; QA's cue count of late fires and refusals shows it.

statement: RT + B stays a signature for as long as the fighter is not channelling, not for 12 ticks, because the rule reads state and not time.
depends_on: F-COMBAT-02 (it goes away when RT + B is replaced)

statement: Transformations are the shared three-tier ladder for both fighters: the Protagonist's own forms are switched off, the rival has none, and the only per-tier look is an aura with placeholder poses.
risk: Turning the Protagonist's own steps on without a matching set for the rival breaks the two-fighter balance; a mirror batch per fighter shows it.
depends_on: data/fight has no owns line; placed with Game Design, who wrote the forms rules the data cites

statement: In Orb's last full match the player's fighter never left tier 1 while the computer reached tier 3; the transform chord has no hint.
risk: The cause is not evidenced (no hint, power too slow for a player, or the chord unread); one replay read of slot 0's power and transform edges settles it.

statement: A body that hits a building still bounces back; the settings that would hold it are one switch row held off waiting on a QA read.
risk: A held body can trap a fight inside a tower with the camera outside; QA's city read is the early check.

statement: No tool measures X-03, X-04, X-13 or X-16, and X-17's trace tool has no count.
risk: Probes written before the move table is agreed will measure the wrong cells.

statement: Launches are not physics-based: the meteor is an authored curve and no attack has a force or any fighter a weight.
evidence: git grep -i kinetic|heft -- sim data: no result
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the physics packet gives no build total that was read here)
risk: It touches every launch and crater number at once.
orb_question: Physics-based launches in Alpha or after? Recommendation: after; for Alpha only a force per attack and a weight per fighter in data.

statement: Chaining hits on a flying foe is only the tap chase; the LT chase, a chain window after a knock-back and a midair flurry are off or absent.
A live transformation blocks new exchanges but damage has no transformation guard, so 'respected' is not proven for shots already in flight.
evidence: sim/core/damage.gd (grep for breakIn, formReady, transform, SimPause: no result)

statement: Backburnered systems still act in the director: menace adds to beam clash power, both meters steer a deflected beam, biome variants shape the signature's aftermath, and hiding code runs inert.
Only 5 of 65 director checks run in CI; the beam, stick, stance and brawl checks run only on a local stack that is not in the repository.
Two planned-exchange templates have a single outcome, and all templates key on the retired four-stance states.
The mixed string's switch reads 'on' in the played build but no game code reads its data file; the feature comes from parked files outside main.
Six of Orb's 'workshop this' combat items have no decision: beam stages, the timed swat, the catch, what RT held does, the taunt before a signature, and whose stick moves whom up close.
orb_question: How much gravity well is enough for Alpha? Recommendation: size, zones and the snap; the far kit and the catch, swat and taunt after Alpha.

statement: Each fighter has his own pools for all nine ways to press X, Y and B in the close fight.
The stick beam is its own staged move, aimed by the stick, and a shot wider than the assist misses and carves; on in the played build.
A player's B alone no longer starts a beam where the fix is on: six of slot 0's eight beams in Orb's last match came from RB and the stick.
A transformation starts only between exchanges and its full and short versions freeze the whole sim.
The energy row exists: bolts and volleys on RB + X, a charged shot on RB + Y, and the Driver on RB + B.
A launch now goes the way of the blow unless the stick picks the far side, behind a switch that is on in the played build.
The tap chase after a launch is built and is checked in CI.
